checks.tolerance: Compilation and resource bundling only; signing, notarization and clean-user installation are separate tasks (T-T02).

Headless startup must exit before NSApplication finishes launching and still deliver the deferred focus sample; a nonzero exit or a missing report fails this check. The source scene supplies object key 10 for the controlled motion profile. The adapter report and focus events are capture-only (A06): IKKOKU_AUTOCAPTURE ends the run, and the app rejects the report without it. The Studio PNG proves only that the run completed. The source scene needs the original avatar, declared here: an automated run ignores the saved library selection, and the source-tree fallback (.local/reverse/rigs/source-avatar.json) exists only in the main checkout, so from a worktree the check failed with "Export the original clothed avatar before previewing source scenes" (2026-11-19).

#459: a performance-trace launch imports its scene in the background, like an interactive one, and the launch-time plug-in profile must mount once that import commits (before #459 it bound to the empty document and the commit dropped it). Not a timing measurement: the trace only carries the launch record (details.launchStudioExecution) that studio-launch-plugins-validate reads; its frame timings are not compared, so it needs no quiet window. The scene and profile are startup-mute-capture's, without that capture's adapter manifest, focus events and report, which only a capture accepts.

Validates studio-launch-plugins-perf's trace (#459): the launch inputs ran after the background import (appliedAfterImport), IKKOKU_SOURCE_PLUGIN_PROFILE among them, at least one plug-in package mounted and one character built, and the startup scene ready. Main 5289f4bc, before the fix, fails it.

Runs the Debug app so the Studio source-pose inspector writes the report at IKKOKU_CAPTURE_UI_REPORT, which must then validate (see studio-inspector-validate). IKKOKU_MAKER_LIBRARY=none keeps a developer's optional converted Maker library (found through the source-tree fallback) out of the synthetic scene's import; with it, the synthetic character imported as no source character and nothing was selected (2026-10-23). The window PNG is hashed only to prove the capture wrote a nonempty file (the app itself verifies it decodes at the captured size, A-T05); cacheDisplay omits most SwiftUI content (ST-D07), so the PNG is not inspector evidence.
Validates the report produced by studio-inspector-capture; until the PR #5 app hooks exist, nothing writes that JSON, so this check fails on the absent report — exactly as intended.

#333 through the UI capture path, the start of #319's ui-sel-clothes capture, where the Clothes tab was laid out wider than the inspector in 6 of 10 launches before the fix (the inspector's scroll view ran past the window's trailing edge): the Debug app starts on the Clothes tab, selects character 0, folder 622 and character 963, and captures, with legacy scrollers for the app process only (-AppleShowScrollBars Always in the argument domain, not System Settings). The fit log (IKKOKU_CAPTURE_UI_FIT_LOG, one launch per file) is judged by studio-inspector-clothes-fit-validate; this check only needs the capture, its report and the log to be written.

Validates the fit log of studio-inspector-clothes-fit-capture: exactly one captured line, showing character 963 on the Clothes tab, with the inspector's document view no wider than its clip view and the accessibility fit check after the capture passing (InspectorFitRule). A log without the inspector's scroll view, the state of #333's bad captures, fails. With --pose-picker (#363), the toolbar's pose-mode picker must also be laid out at its intrinsic width at the capture (the fit log's layout probe): under a fixed frame narrower than the control it was laid out compressed on a fresh build and at full width on a rebuild, as here after the folder selection. With --toolbar-fits (#425), the toolbar must fit this window without its scroll view in Object, FK and IK mode (full or compact variant, by the ideal widths the app logs after the capture), and show the first variant that fits the state shown.

#366 through the UI capture path, #366's ui-sel-chars start: the Debug app starts on the Object tab, selects character 0 then character 963, and captures. The fit log (IKKOKU_CAPTURE_UI_FIT_LOG, one launch per file) is judged by studio-inspector-object-heights-validate; this check only needs the capture, its report and the log to be written.

Validates the fit log of studio-inspector-object-heights-capture: one captured line showing character 963 on the Object tab, the inspector fit as for every capture, and with --object-heights 24 21 (#366's R2 on this machine) the explicit text-field heights the inspector lays out with (InspectorTextFieldHeight, measured from an AppKit prototype with SwiftUI's bezel and font) at 24 pt for the Name field and 21 pt for the Transform fields, equal to SwiftUI's own fields: the Name field's intrinsic height 24 pt and every other editable field's 21 pt. Frame heights are not judged: in about 1% of launches the Name field is still laid out 21 pt inside its 24 pt slot (#366's residue, which stays open).

Builds the optimized app that release-startup-capture launches. The flags match the CI release-package job, except that signing stays on. Debug lanes cannot catch optimizer-only faults: on 2026-10-23 every Release render crashed while all Debug lanes passed (R6, FrameRing.allocate(array:)).

Release smoke: renders the bundled public Maker character once and exits 0 with a nonempty PNG. Source-tree fallbacks are off and the saved converted library is ignored in an automated run, so only bundled assets are used and no fixture is needed. Before the R6 fix (2026-10-23, Xcode 27.0 / Swift 6.4) this run crashed with SIGSEGV in Renderer.prepare on the first skinned frame. The PNG proves only that one optimized frame rendered and was written; it is not a visual reference.

Runs the FrameRing tests optimized; a cold build takes about four minutes. frameRingArrayAllocationReachesAThrowingCallerWithoutAnError calls allocate(array:) from a throwing caller. Before the R6 fix, this release run ended with signal 11; the Debug suite passed. GPU cases need a Metal device.
